texts.li: [fire,lowtech] A fire started in a bakehouse at {PLACE} and went through the thatch faster than the bucket lines could follow. A quarter of the town is ash, and {FACTION} are sleeping under carts and in the temple.\n\n{DEAD}, who speaks for the town now, has sent a rider to the colony with a list: what they need to rebuild before the weather turns, and what they'll pay for it.

[fire,!lowtech] A letter from {DEAD} at {PLACE}, written fast:\n\n"The fuel store went up on the third night of the dry spell and took the whole of Mill Street with it. Every family {FACTION} could fit is sleeping in the school hall. We are rebuilding now, before the weather turns, and we can pay. The list is enclosed. I'd be grateful for a quick answer."

[storm,lowtech] A storm came down the valley two nights ago and took the roofs off half of {PLACE}. {FACTION} saved what they could; the rest went down the river.\n\n{DEAD} has sent a rider to ask whether the colony can sell them what they need to put the roofs back on, by a set day.

[storm,!lowtech] The windstorm that tore through {PLACE} two nights ago took roofs, walls and the power lines in the street. {FACTION} are patching what they can with tarps and rope.\n\n{DEAD}, who's in charge of the rebuilding, has sent a list to the colony, and a fair price for all of it.

[flood] The river came up over its banks at {PLACE} and stood in the streets for three days. The lower town is mud to the windowsills, and {FACTION} are digging out with shovels and buckets.\n\n{DEAD} has sent word to the colony: they need building materials, and food for the work crews, by a set day, and they'll pay well for them.

li.label: Accept the terms
li.outcome: The messenger left at once, to tell them help is coming.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: {FACTION} will have to look elsewhere for their timber.

terms.li: {FACTION}'s list: {ITEM}, all of it in the colony's stockpiles within {DAYS} of the colony agreeing.\n\nFor everything, they'll pay {COUNT} silver, well over its worth. With at least half of each thing ready, they'll take what there is at its plain worth. Less than that, and they'll go elsewhere, and remember it.

accepted.li: [fire] {PLACE} will rebuild with the colony's help: {ITEM}, ready within {DAYS}, for {FACTION}'s carts to collect.
[storm] The colony has promised {PLACE} what it needs to get its roofs back on: {ITEM}, within {DAYS}. {FACTION} will send carts.
[flood] The colony will help {PLACE} dig out. {FACTION}'s carts come for {ITEM} within {DAYS}.

ready.li: Everything {PLACE} needs to rebuild is ready, and {FACTION}'s carts are due in {DAYS}.
[fire] The timber and the rest for {PLACE} are stacked and waiting, and {FACTION}'s carts are due within {DAYS}.
[flood] Everything {PLACE} needs to dig out and build again is ready. If the roads have dried, {FACTION}'s carts will be here in {DAYS}.

reminder.li: {FACTION}'s carts come for the building materials within {DAYS}, and the stockpiles are still short: {ITEM}.
[storm] {PLACE} still has sky where its roofs should be. {FACTION}'s carts come within {DAYS} for {ITEM}.
[fire] {PLACE} is still living in tents among the ashes, and {FACTION}'s carts come within {DAYS} for {ITEM}.

done.li: [delivered,fire] Everything the colony had set aside went home on {FACTION}'s carts, and {DEAD} sent {ITEM} silver back with the drivers. The new houses at {PLACE} will have the colony's timber in their walls.
[delivered,storm] The materials went home piled high on {FACTION}'s carts. {DEAD} sent {ITEM} silver with them, and word that the roofs at {PLACE} will be on before the next storm.

[delivered,flood] {FACTION}'s carts took everything the colony had set aside, and {DEAD} sent {ITEM} silver back with them. The work crews at {PLACE} are eating the colony's food while they shovel the mud out of their neighbors' houses.
[partial] Only part of the list was ready when {FACTION}'s carts came. They took it, paid its plain worth, {ITEM} silver, and went on looking for the rest.

fail.li: [missed] {FACTION}'s carts came for the materials and went back empty; there was far too little ready to be worth the trip. {PLACE} will rebuild slower than it hoped, and {FACTION} think less of the colony for it.

[missed,fire] {FACTION}'s carts came for the timber and left with almost nothing. The burned street at {PLACE} will stand empty a while longer, and {DEAD} has said so, in a letter the colony would rather not have received.

cancelled.li: {FACTION} are no longer on terms with the colony, and the order for {PLACE} is off.
{FACTION} have broken with the colony. {PLACE} will have to rebuild with someone else's help.

texts.li: [winter,lowtech] {DEAD}, who keeps the stores at {PLACE}, has counted twice and come out short both times. The harvest came in thin, and {FACTION} won't have enough laid by to see the winter out.\n\nA rider has brought the colony {DEAD}'s list: food that keeps, firewood, and cloth or hides for winter coats, all by a set day.

[winter,!lowtech] {FACTION}'s granary at {PLACE} took water in the autumn rains, and half of it spoiled before anyone noticed the smell. {DEAD}, their quartermaster, has sent a courier with a list of what they'll need to get through the winter, and a good price for all of it.

[drought] The rains failed at {PLACE} this year. The wells are low, the fields are dust, and {FACTION} are eating their seed grain.\n\n{DEAD} has sent a rider to the colony: they need food, and medicine for the fevers that come with bad water, and they'll pay what they can.

[sickness,lowtech] A sickness is going round {PLACE}, the kind that keeps people in bed for a week and leaves them weak. {DEAD}, their healer, has turned the meeting hall into a sickhouse and sent to the colony for medicine, food and clean cloth.

[sickness,!lowtech] {FACTION}'s clinic at {PLACE} is full. A bad flu, {DEAD} writes, nothing worse, but enough to empty the shelves; the order that came by courier asks for medicine, meals for the patients and cloth for bandages and bedding, by a set day.

li.label: Accept the terms
li.outcome: The messenger left with the colony's promise and a full water skin.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: {FACTION} will have to look elsewhere, and hope.

terms.li: {FACTION} are asking for {ITEM}, in the colony's stockpiles within {DAYS} of the colony agreeing, with any food still fresh when the carts come.\n\nAll of it fetches {COUNT} silver, well over its worth. At least half of each thing, and they'll take what there is at its plain worth. Less, and they'll go elsewhere, and remember it.

accepted.li: [winter] {PLACE} will get through the winter on the colony's stores: {ITEM}, ready within {DAYS} for {FACTION}'s carts.
[drought] The colony will have food and medicine ready for {PLACE} within {DAYS}: {ITEM}. {FACTION} will send carts.
[sickness] {DEAD}'s sickhouse at {PLACE} will have the colony's supplies within {DAYS}: {ITEM}, collected by {FACTION}'s carts.

ready.li: Everything {PLACE} asked for is ready, and {FACTION}'s carts are due in {DAYS}.
[winter] The winter stores for {PLACE} are packed and waiting for {FACTION}'s carts, due in {DAYS}.
[sickness] The supplies for {DEAD}'s sickhouse are packed, the medicine wrapped twice. {FACTION}'s carts are due within {DAYS}.

reminder.li: Within {DAYS}, {FACTION}'s carts come for the provisions: {ITEM}.
[drought] {PLACE} is counting the days until the colony's food arrives. {FACTION}'s carts come within {DAYS} for {ITEM}.
[sickness] {DEAD}'s sickhouse at {PLACE} is waiting on the colony for {ITEM}, and {FACTION}'s carts come within {DAYS}.

done.li: [delivered,winter] The winter stores went off to {PLACE} on {FACTION}'s carts, and {DEAD} sent {ITEM} silver without haggling over a single sack. {PLACE} will see the winter out.
[delivered,drought] The food and medicine went home on {FACTION}'s carts, and {ITEM} silver stayed behind. When the rains come back, {DEAD} says, {PLACE} will still be there to see them.
[delivered,sickness] {FACTION}'s carts took the supplies straight to {DEAD}'s sickhouse at {PLACE}, and the drivers left {ITEM} silver and a note from {DEAD}: "We'll manage now. Thank you."
[partial] Half loaded, {FACTION}'s carts went home with what the colony had ready, and left {ITEM} silver for its plain worth. The rest will have to come from somewhere else.

fail.li: [missed] {FACTION}'s carts came and found far too little ready, and went home empty. {PLACE} will have to find what it needs elsewhere, if it can.
[missed,sickness] There was almost nothing for {FACTION}'s carts to take. {DEAD} sent one line back with the drivers: the sickhouse would manage without the colony, as it always had.

cancelled.li: {FACTION} are no longer on terms with the colony, and the order for {PLACE} is off.
{FACTION} have broken with the colony, and {PLACE} will have to find its provisions elsewhere.
